headline: Google DeepMind says it has seen no measurable speed-up in AI research caused by AI itself, even though AI now writes most of its code.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: first-hand data from a leading lab on a much-debated question, but self-reported.
summary: The Decoder reports that Haydn Belfield, an engineer at Google DeepMind, says the lab sees no measurable acceleration of AI research driven by AI itself, although AI writes more than 75 percent of its production code and about 88 percent of code changes still need human review. The team rates the risk from AI-driven research automation as low for now, which contrasts with a recent warning of a possible 'intelligence explosion' by more than 20 researchers, including Geoffrey Hinton, an emeritus professor at the University of Toronto, and Yoshua Bengio, a professor at the Université de Montréal.
importance_line: Policymakers and the public weighing claims of runaway AI progress get a data point from inside a leading lab, but it is the company's own measurement and may change quickly.
